chapter: Civil service, Keyhole club and civil rights
title: Orrin Blackstone and the first article on Albert
summary: Albert recalls Orrin Blackstone writing the first story about him; they discuss what became of Blackstone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: You were only a year in the post office? That's all I knew. Because you know, I had, Orrin Blackstone had met you, I don't know if you remember him.
Orrin Blackstone was the first one that wrote that article on me. I still have that little book, whether it was Playback or something like that. He was up on Verone Street. Yeah, 439.
That's right. So that's when I just missed you, see I had just come to New Orleans.
And I heard about you through Orrin, because Orrin thought something like that. Right.
But I met him, he came to the house down there. That was the first story that actually came out on me. That was the first.
Well, he's very few people know about Orrin today.
He met Mr. Slidell, and he's a newspaper man, and he's retired.

You know, I sure would like to write him a letter. If you get by chance, can talk to him or send me his address. I have it with me. Well, good, we'll get it before you leave. I know he'd be surprised. I haven't talked to him since he wrote the story.
Yeah. Well, of course, he and I went in the record business together. Oh, you did?
